item.title: Jamming is a much bigger problem than we think
item.description: Last month, a Russian Kosmos military satellite came within a few hundred metres of an American commercial satellite operated by ICEYE. The ICEYE satellite provides imagery to Ukraine’s armed forces. The incident elicited warnings from Washington and renewed fears that Russia might attack Western satellites in orbit. If anyone outside Moscow knows what the Russian spacecraft was doing, they haven’t made it public, although the movements of the Kosmos spacecraft were plainly deliberate. The prospect of hostile satellites chasing one another through space is certainly alarming. But military planners have another, less conspicuous threat to contend with, and good reason to suspect that it is far more widespread than we have been led to believe.
